category: Enterprise Architecture, System Hardening & Advanced Threats

content.tldr: Micro-segmentation divides data centers and cloud workloads into isolated, granular security segments down to individual workloads, enforcing strict east-west traffic policies.
content.simple_explanation: Traditional network security focused on north-south traffic (traffic entering or leaving the perimeter via edge firewalls), leaving internal east-west traffic (communication between servers inside the same VLAN) largely unmonitored. Micro-segmentation applies software-defined security policies directly to individual virtual machines, containers, or Kubernetes pods using host-based firewalls (iptables, eBPF) or cloud Security Groups, permitting only authorized service-to-service communication.
content.real_world_example: Watertight bulkheads inside a submarine: if one compartment floods with seawater, sealed doors prevent the water from cascading into adjacent compartments, keeping the vessel afloat.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Without micro-segmentation, compromising a single low-security web server allows an attacker to pivot unimpeded across the internal network to payment databases. Micro-segmentation confines breaches to their immediate workload.
